entry.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
entry.summary:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ρ,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ρ(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ρ$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

entry.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
entry.summary: Random projection is a basic compression primitive for Euclidean representation learning, with the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma giving a target dimension $k=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ independent of the ambient dimension. As hyperbolic representations gain increasing attention in modern Transformers, vision-language models, and large language models, the same need for oblivious dimensionality reduction arises, but no analogous primitive yet exists for hyperbolic representations. We study this gap. Two natural attempts fail in dual ways: a tangent-space scheme gives a clean local guarantee but is chart-bound and pays a curvature penalty, while a fully hyperbolic projection in the hyperboloid model is geometrically native but mixes radial and angular error before feeding them into the conditioning of $\operatorname{arcosh}$. We propose radial-angular random projection (RAP), which preserves the radial coordinate exactly and applies a Euclidean random projection only to the angular direction, lifting the result back to the target hyperboloid. RAP is hyperbolic-to-hyperbolic by construction, costs one Gaussian matrix-vector product, and reduces hyperbolic compression to a normalized angular JL question on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. We prove a finite-set RAP guarantee with explicit $\sinh(\sqrt{c}\,r_x)\sinh(\sqrt{c}\,r_y)$ conditioning, complemented by a local tangent-space JL theorem and an arcosh-conditioning lemma for the fully hyperbolic comparator. Across an origin-centered broad-radius point cloud, a balanced tree, a clustered Gaussian, and the WordNet noun hierarchy, RAP attains the lowest mean relative distortion in every $(n,k)$ cell, reducing distortion over the strongest hyperbolic baseline by approximately $48\%$--$49\%$ on broad-radius data. RAP also scales to million-point datasets and improves retrieval on vision--language representations over hyperbolic projection baselines.
entry.arxiv:comment: 39 pages, 11 figures, 15 tables, including appendices

entry.title: LatENSO v1.0: a learned latent state of the tropical Pacific for seasonal ENSO operators and forecasting
entry.summary: Here we present LatENSO v1.0, a machine-learning forecast system for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) built around a learned, 32-dimensional state of the tropical Pacific. A Swin-transformer autoencoder compresses thirteen monthly-averaged ocean and atmosphere fields into 32 numbers, trained to reconstruct the fields, with no forecast target. The 32 numbers rebuild the fields as well as O(100) empirical orthogonal functions. Two seasonal operators use this state. The first is the extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO) with two directions of the learned state among its variables; we call it XRO-lat. The second is a Floquet modal operator (FMO) of three damped oscillators, which forecasts a correction added to a least-squares base forecast made from four observed predictors. We evaluate both against the recharge oscillator, XRO and a deep echo-state network (DESN), all refitted on identical data, cross-validation folds and verification windows (1981-2024). Over lead times of 1-18 months, XRO-lat reaches an anomaly correlation coefficient (ACC) of 0.673, the highest of all tropical-Pacific-only (in-domain) systems and statistically indistinguishable from XRO and DESN with their eight remote-basin indices (0.685 and 0.667). From lead 15 to lead 24 it is the most skillful of all systems. Over leads 1-18, the FMO forecast (0.619) is statistically indistinguishable from every in-domain reference model (0.631-0.654). What the FMO adds to its base forecast, 0.054 in ACC, is carried by its Floquet propagation, whose generator consistently holds a prominent quasi-biennial oscillator. At leads 3-9 the FMO trails XRO, DESN and the in-domain XRO, a deficit partly attributable to its base. LatENSO combines competitive skill with trustworthiness: a compact state whose physical content can be inspected, and fully open access to code, weights and data.
entry.arxiv:comment: 61 pages, 14 figures. Submitted to Geoscientific Model Development

entry.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
entry.summary: Although multimodal large language models translate single screenshots into static HTML, generating interactive functional websites from design specifications still struggles with multi-page routing and stateful widget transitions. Examining existing training pipelines reveals two bottlenecks: (1) in forward data synthesis (X -> Y), writing the specification X before code execution leaves unimplemented or altered requirements in X as supervision noise; and (2) in reinforcement learning, scalar rewards discard the rich state transitions observed during replay. Based on these findings, we introduce WebVibe and Interactive-SDPO to train InteractiveCoder. WebVibe reverses synthesis into Y -> X by verifying cross-page and in-page interactions in the browser before deriving multimodal inputs from replay-confirmed states to build the 31,542-site WebVibe-32K corpus with reusable execution contracts. Interactive-SDPO then conditions a weight-sharing self-teacher on the replay trace and a 2x2 state-transition montage to provide token-level supervision at zero inference-time overhead. On the public Vision2Web L2, one-shot InteractiveCoder-9B nearly 3x its base model's functional score (20.2 to 55.2 FS) and matches a 1T-parameter coding agent in a single pass with 111x fewer total parameters and 78x fewer tokens. On our WebVibeBench, InteractiveCoder-4B and 9B further outperform all evaluated baselines by over 23 points.

entry.title: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms
entry.summary: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that involve parameterised quantum circuits and classical optimisation. VQAs have found applications in simulation, optimisation, and machine learning. However, their scalability is hindered by flat landscapes-regions in the parameter space where gradients vanish exponentially small. In such regimes, gradient-based optimisation methods fail because parameter updates become ineffective in the absence of informative gradients. In this work, we propose a search-based restart framework to escape flat regions in structured flat landscapes, in which small trainable regions exist within a large flat landscape. This framework approaches the plateau escape as a search problem and locates trainable regions. The optimiser's parameters stop updating when the gradients vanish, and the method then searches over-sampled points to identify landscapes with nonzero gradients. We provide theoretical estimates of the number of jumps and the probability of escape from flat landscapes. This restarts the local optimisation process and avoids stagnation. We tested this framework on synthetic functions that mimic structured flat landscapes and a real quantum circuit cost landscape. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that Search-for-Gradient improves optimisation performance in structured flat landscapes. The proposed framework assumes the existence of a trainable region with nonzero measure and will not work if it has zero measure. Our framework can be integrated with existing VQAs to improve trainability and robustness.

entry.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
entry.summary: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes. Confirmed generation results are linked to the corresponding asset states, story time, and reference versions for verification and reuse by subsequent shots. Hierarchical Collaboration isolates execution contexts by task, clip, and repair round, and uses hierarchical memory to organize this process across multiple sets. Across multiple benchmarks, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods and produces long videos with sustained cross-shot consistency under predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.

entry.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary: As large language models increasingly collaborate in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, latent communication has emerged as an efficient alternative to exchanging natural-language messages. By sharing internal representations, agents can avoid repeatedly processing the same context, reducing communication overhead and prefill computation. One such mechanism is cross-model Key-Value (KV) cache transfer, which uses a learned mapper to translate a source model's KV cache into one a target model can use. However, this handoff means the target model consumes context it did not encode itself, thus calling into question whether its safety alignment still holds. In this work, we investigate the security implications of latent handoffs by introducing Chasm, a framework characterizing cross-model handoff attacks across three new attack surfaces: the source model, mapper, and handoff mechanism itself. Our experiments reveal that latent handoffs substantially undermine safety alignment and prompt-injection defenses. Notably, a target model that follows only 0.4% of benchmark prompt injections natively, follows up to 44.2% when transferred through a mapper from a source model. On the other hand, for jailbreak attacks, transfer alone raises attack success by up to 24.6 pp within a model family and zero-shot attacks by up to 69.2 pp, whereas white-box optimization through the mapper boosts the attack success rate to 92.5%, against 37.5% for ordinary GCG on the same target. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose a lightweight target-side cache guard that corrects transferred caches to restore the target model's refusal, considerably mitigating these attacks.

entry.title: Beat This! Live - Online Beat and Downbeat Tracking by Predicting the Future
entry.summary: Beat and downbeat tracking have seen multiple improvements through recent deep learning approaches, but most target an offline setting, precluding their use in real-time scenarios. We adapt a recent offline beat tracking model, Beat This, for online, low-latency operation and propose Beat This! Live, a causal variant designed for real-time beat and downbeat tracking. We present the architectural modifications required to obtain a causal system suitable for streaming inference and measure their impact on accuracy. By training our model with temporally shifted labels, it produces predictions slightly ahead of the current frame, which not only reduces latency, but enables much more effective peak-picking. Evaluation on the GTZAN dataset shows the F1-score improves from 80.6 to 86.7 for beats and 56.5 to 74.1 for downbeats compared to BeatNet+, the current state of the art in online beat tracking.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted at the 27th International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR), 2026

entry.title: Scaling Looped MoE Language Models under Matched Budgets: Information Flow and Parameter Allocation
entry.summary: Looped Transformers decouple computational depth from parameter count, and prior studies have demonstrated promising performance gains with increased computation. However, systematic design principles for configuring these models under strict iso-parameter and iso-FLOP constraints remain scarce. We contribute to this direction by improving information flow in looped models and systematically studying loop parameter configurations. Specifically, we refine this information flow via gated inner-loop state updates and a cross-stage residual connection. Building on this design, controlled studies identify a configuration combining a single-pass Core depth of 25%-35% of the total unrolled depth with reallocating saved parameters into extra routed experts per layer, improving performance at zero extra compute while preserving compatibility with existing training infrastructure. Evaluated after 1T pre-training tokens, our 69B MLA and 51B KDA Mixture-of-Experts models outperform budget-matched non-recurrent baselines by an average of 1.16 and 2.29 percentage points across four benchmarks, respectively. Further reproduction experiments on a common backbone with a 200B-token training budget show that our method achieves lower perplexity than other looped methods. Code for these reproduction experiments is available at https://github.com/lxi01766/Scaling-Looped-MoE-Language-Models-under-Matched-Budgets-Information-Flow-and-Parameter-Allocation.

entry.title: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees
entry.summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns a response policy from human preference data, but with a limited dataset it can overfit to noisy or weakly informative preference labels. We introduce LatentCP-DPO, a framework that combines conformal prediction with pessimistic preference optimization for Bradley-Terry (BT) pairwise feedback and Plackett-Luce (PL) ranking feedback. Building on LatentCP's construction of uncertainty sets for unobserved model parameters, we address how to incorporate this uncertainty into preference optimization and characterize its effect on policy performance. Under exchangeability and a correctly specified preference model, we construct uncertainty sets for latent relative rewards with finite-sample marginal coverage from conformal prediction sets for observable preferences. We then learn a response policy by maximizing the worst-case expected preference log-likelihood over these uncertainty sets, using an independent collection of prompts and candidate responses without preference labels. Under suitable assumptions, we establish finite-sample upper bounds on regularized policy suboptimality that separate policy-class approximation error, conformal uncertainty, and statistical estimation error. For BT feedback, we further establish a worst-case lower bound for LatentCP-DPO that matches the upper bound's reciprocal dependence on the number of unlabeled optimization examples. The lower bound also shows that the uncertainty sets can induce a bias that persists as the optimization sample grows. Together, these results characterize both the statistical accuracy and potential limitations of preference optimization using conformal uncertainty sets. Experiments support the benefits of the proposed framework in finite preference datasets.
entry.arxiv:comment: 62 Pages

entry.title: Libtt: A Compiler and Runtime for Tenstorrent Processors
entry.summary: Libtt brings the PyTorch and JAX ecosystem to Tenstorrent hardware. It implements PJRT, the interface through which XLA-based frameworks drive Google's TPUs, so JAX runs on it directly, PyTorch runs through TorchTPU, and software written for TPUs carries over with no changes except replacing custom kernels. Built on Tenstorrent's open-source compiler and runtime, libtt ships the entire stack, from the compiler to the multi-chip runtime, as a single shared library. It contains extensive fixes to the upstream Tenstorrent software to make existing PyTorch and JAX code work out of the box, and extensive new compiler optimizations to make it fast. It passes most of the JAX and TorchTPU test suites and runs SGLang, TorchTitan, and Miles, covering serving, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.
entry.arxiv:comment: 28 pages, 5 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/pcmoritz/libtt

entry.title: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining
entry.summary: Interpretable tool wear assessment in CNC machining is challenging. Existing diagnostic models have high accuracy but provide limited guidance for tool replacement. This study proposes a two layer framework combining deep learning wear classification and LLM assisted reasoning. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and optimized GRU to recognize three wear states, achieving 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation shows the reports outperform rule templates. Cross dataset tests on NASA milling data support the generalizability of this framework.

entry.title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
entry.summary: We present a quantum algorithm for the early fault-tolerant quantum computing (early-FTQC) era that estimates minute energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces, at a lower sampling cost than existing phase-estimation methods. Such energy derivatives, accessed as the small energy difference induced by an infinitesimal parameter shift, are central to quantum simulation in chemistry and materials science. Although Statistical Phase Estimation (SPE) is well-suited to energy estimation in this era, applying it to an energy difference demands a sampling complexity that scales with the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian, which grows with system size. Our algorithm overcomes this by incorporating two time-evolution operators, corresponding to the Hamiltonians before and after the parameter shift, into a single quantum circuit, which is combined with a non-adaptive, statistically sampled reconstruction in the energy-difference domain. This reduces the relevant scale from the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian to that of the operator norm of the Hamiltonian derivative and the parameter shift, thereby lowering the sampling complexity. We further propose the joint estimation of energy eigenvalues and their differences, giving a holistic view of the energy landscape. Numerical simulations and resource estimations on prototypical systems, such as the Fermi-Hubbard model, demonstrate the resulting reductions in required resources without compromising precision. This positions energy-difference estimation as a practical task for early-FTQC devices, opening a route to molecular forces, response properties, and excited-state energy differences.
entry.arxiv:comment: 34 pages, 8 figures

entry.title: Train-Only-Constrained LM for Synthetic Clinical Trajectories: Leak-Safe Calibration and Auditable Dynamics
entry.summary: Simulating clinical time series necessitates temporal realism, calibration that preserves model integrity, and privacy transparency. We present a train-only, constrained language-model pipeline that factorizes generation. A compact GPT-style language model learns cross-biomarker co-occurrence through quantile tokens, and temporal directions are enforced by 3x3 per-biomarker Markov transitions fit on TRAIN, allowing dynamics to be audited. We fit a monotone quantile map (QMap) on TRAIN only (SYN(TRAIN) -> SIM(TRAIN)); no TEST statistics are used. The fixed map is then applied to SYN(TEST) severities. The constrained LM demonstrated improved distributional fidelity and co-occurrence in a 5,000-patient simulated testbed (parameters within published clinical ranges) compared to an empirical sampler, maintained near-chance detectability after a small lambda-sweep, and exhibits temporal adherence by construction. A classifier-based membership-inference audit results in an AUC of approximately 0.5; we make no differential-privacy claim. We present multi-seed results with paired 95% confidence intervals and quantify the severity of QMap's alignment (Delta W1 with confidence interval). This is a Stage-1 method result obtained on a controlled simulator; Stage-2 validation on real EHR cohorts with clinical endpoints is planned.
entry.arxiv:comment: Preprint (pre-review version, 6 pages, 2 figures). Accepted at SECURE AI4H@AAAI 2026, Singapore. Extended version to appear in Springer CCIS vol. 3004 (2027): https://link.springer.com/book/9789819239238

entry.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
entry.summary: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandboxed graders verify the resulting synthesis routes, experimental protocols, and other outputs. Laboratory tasks use robotic simulators or previously measured experimental data. We evaluate 14 LLMs as agents and find that the best achieves an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization emerging as the hardest domains. Overall performance does not predict optimization performance well: the model ranked twelfth overall achieves the highest score in closed-loop optimization. Error analysis also shows that agents often submit chemically invalid results despite running their tools successfully. Stronger models benefit more from tool access, but reliable use of chemical software remains a challenge that Crucible Bench can track as models improve.

entry.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
entry.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to use available skills autonomously. We quantify the EBU gap as the difference in skill-use accuracy between autonomous use and explicitly guided reading and application of the same skill. On EBU-Bench, all evaluated model-harness combinations exhibit EBU, with a mean gap of 43.94 percentage points (pp). For the same model, skill-use accuracy under autonomous use differs by up to 38.96 pp across harnesses. Motivated by these observations, we propose EBU-Evolve, which uses execution feedback from autonomous and explicitly guided skill use to distill effective guidance into reusable skill instructions. Relative to their pre-evolution versions, the revised skills improve skill-use accuracy during autonomous execution by 33.33 to 55.17 pp and continue to yield improvements when transferred across multiple models and harnesses. Our results show that autonomous skill-use accuracy varies across harnesses with the model and skill held fixed, and model rankings can change. EBU can persist even after a skill is opened. EBU-Evolve improves autonomous skill-use accuracy on unseen tasks within the same skill, with gains transferring across models and harnesses.
entry.arxiv:comment: 42 pages,including appendices

entry.title: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
entry.summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) with general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a flexible alternative to task-specific navigation policies, while reliable long-horizon execution remains challenging. Agents must track navigation progress, detect discrepancies between commanded and actual motion, and recognize when movement has passed relevant landmarks or entrances. We present Navigent, an agentic VLN framework built around a frozen MLLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic (GEC). GEC performs two complementary checks: action-to-motion consistency, which evaluates measured displacement against commanded movement, and motion-to-landmark consistency, which tracks agent-selected visual anchors and entrance candidates in world coordinates. Detected discrepancies interrupt the remaining action sequence and trigger reobservation, local adjustment, or node-based recovery. Historical visual memory supports progress tracking across extended routes. An offline self-improvement procedure further analyzes successful and failed training trajectories to refine navigation prompts and GEC logic while keeping model weights fixed. On the R2R-CE validation-unseen split (1,839 episodes) and RxR-CE validation-unseen split(3,669 episodes), Navigent achieves 84.0%/86.0% SR and 72.9%/69.1% SPL, respectively, demonstrating the value of geometry-grounded execution verification for reliable agentic navigation. Project Page: https://marslab-navigent.github.io/navigent.github.io/ Code: https://github.com/MarsLab-Navigent/Navigent

entry.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Shapley values in reinforcement learning are used to explain which observation features drive an agent's behavior and expected return, but not its certainty. Explaining certainty requires understanding how observation features influence different sources of return uncertainty, and Shapley values need the agent's prediction for every subset of visible features. We propose EXPOSURE, which uses one mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley explanations. It explains the variance of the return, split into an observational part due to missing features and an inherent part due to the environment's own randomness, and the entropy of its belief over the masked features. In tic-tac-toe and Minesweeper, where exact Shapley values are computable, EXPOSURE gives more accurate explanations of expected return and its uncertainty, while uniquely explaining belief uncertainty.
entry.arxiv:comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ESANN 2027. Code: https://github.com/kianaf/exposure-rl

entry.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
entry.summary: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before the decision adds at most a small gain, before or after the models' training cutoffs. The newest graph raises five of six models clearly above that baseline, but its paths usually include the answer: the pair's own trial, dated after the decision. Evaluations of target prioritisation should date both features and labels, with evidence from before the decision and outcomes after it.
entry.arxiv:comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery: Bridging the Translation Gap (AI4DD). Code and data: https://github.com/jackysiupuichung/forecast-or-know

entry.title: Ancilla-Assisted Accelerated Readout of Transmon Qubits
entry.summary: We present a scheme for accelerating dispersive readout of superconducting transmon qubits. Dispersive readout works by weakly coupling the target transmon to a resonator, such that the resonator experiences a state-dependent frequency shift, which can then be read out. Our scheme introduces an ancillary transmon coupled to the same resonator. By appropriately correlating its state with that of the target transmon (using a fast CNOT gate), we show that the resonator frequency shift is approximately doubled, halving the required measurement duration to maintain the same quality. We present analytical results within the dispersive approximation, before employing and extending the recently introduced technique of branch analysis to account for ionization and other nonlinearities. Using this, and taking into account realistic noise and gate times, we show that our scheme allows measurement durations smaller by a factor of approximately 0.6, demonstrating that it offers a viable route for accelerating measurements of transmon qubits.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages, 3 figures

entry.title: Weakly Conditioned Diffusion Model Augmentation for Prostate Segmentation
entry.summary: Deep learning models for prostate MRI segmentation often struggle to generalize when trained on limited heterogeneous data, leading to boundary errors and over-segmentation. We present an augmentation framework using mask-conditioned synthetic and diverse T2-weighted MRI volumes to improve boundary precision and reduce over-segmentation. We employ a 2.5D weakly mask-conditioned denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) via channel concatenation. The diffusion model conditions on stacks of adjacent binary masks from training folds. The model generates T2 volumes consistent with the conditioning anatomy while diversifying tissue appearance. We evaluate the proposed approach on two cohorts of data: (i) the LUND probe cohort (n=432) for strategy selection and training nnU-Net from scratch with a 23% synthetic data mix, and (ii) the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) prostate cohort (n=32) evaluated with a 20% synthetic data mix. For the LUND cohort, we found that training an nnU-Net model from scratch with a 23% synthetic data mix reduced the mean false-positive voxels per case from 11,102 (baseline) to 10,757. On the MSD cohort, the augmented model with a 20% synthetic mix achieved a mean cross-validated Dice of 0.9094, improving over the baseline (0.8935) by 1.59 percentage points and reducing mean false-positive voxels by 23.1% (4,201 to 3,229). Experimental results on both these cohorts suggest that mask-conditioned DDPM augmentation can reduce over-segmentation errors and improve boundary adherence in data-constrained settings.
entry.arxiv:comment: 15 pages, preprint

entry.title: Change Point Detection with Generative Models
entry.summary: Change point detection (CPD) methods aim to identify abrupt changes in the properties of time series, which is a key problem in numerous fields. A major class of CPD approaches relies on computing a CPD score, which is either a discrepancy or divergence between two subsequent samples, called windows. A fundamental limitation of window-based CPD is the 'sample size bottleneck.' To ensure temporal precision, windows must be small; however, small samples provide insufficient statistical evidence for the classifiers and deep-learning models currently used to compute CPD scores. This leads to high variance in the scores and frequent mispredictions. Our study tackles this issue by exploring generative models for window augmentation, effectively expanding available data to improve CPD quality. Experiments on synthetic and real data demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly enhances CPD. Specifically, we show that this approach allows simple classifiers to outperform complex deep-learning baselines by stabilizing the CPD score distribution.
entry.arxiv:comment: Neuroinformatics 2026 (Oral)

entry.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
entry.summary: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification. In human-AI research partnerships, confidence can therefore outgrow evidence through three mechanisms: recursive reinforcement, loss of provenance and miscalibrated reliance on AI-generated contributions. Verification debt accumulates when such contributions are carried into later claims or decisions without adequate scrutiny. Accordingly, we propose the Socratic Pause as a deliberate checkpoint at consequential decision gates, where an AI contribution remains provisional while a researcher examines its basis. The PAUSE protocol structures this examination through five steps: Pin down the claim, Ask and challenge, Uncover assumptions and alternatives, Scrutinise the evidence and Exercise judgement. It concludes with a recorded decision to accept, revise, reject or defer the contribution. We show how AI research tools can support this practice without displacing human judgement, and outline a framework for evaluating whether it improves verification, decision-making and independent understanding. The aim is to preserve the freedom to explore with AI while ensuring that those responsible for the work can say what was examined, what remains uncertain and why the next step is justified.

entry.title: GeoCAM: Self-Supervised Sonar-Optical Representation Learning via Geographic Overlap Supervision
entry.summary: Cross-modal self-supervised learning for paired side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery is a promising direction for benthic habitat understanding, but it remains underexplored because existing methods do not fully exploit the one-to-many correspondences and geographic metadata available in real opti-acoustic surveys. This limits the ability to learn representations that are both semantically meaningful and geometrically consistent from abundant unlabeled marine data. To address this problem, we present GeoCAM, a geography-guided framework that learns a shared embedding space for sonar tiles and their associated optical views without semantic annotations. GeoCAM achieves its goal by combining three components: (i) a Set Attention Aggregator that adaptively summarizes multiple optical observations into a single tile-level representation; (ii) a geometry-weighted InfoNCE objective that converts GPS-derived footprint overlap into soft positive supervision; and (iii) an optional cross-modal masked reconstruction branch that encourages physically grounded cross-modal alignment. Experiments on the BenthiCat SSS-CAM dataset show that GeoCAM can be effectively exploited to learn which sonar and camera samples describe the same seabed patch, improving cross-modal retrieval and alignment over strong contrastive baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/FadiZidiDz/GeoCAM.
entry.arxiv:comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the IEEE International Conference on Advanced Visual and Signal-Based Systems (AVSS 2026)

entry.title: Geometry, masking and selection in Differential Evolution and SOMA on quantum state manifolds
entry.summary: Differential Evolution (DE) and the Self-Organizing Migrating Algorithm (SOMA) generate new candidates through vector arithmetic: they subtract population members, scale the difference, and mask coordinates. Many practical search spaces are not vector spaces, however. Rotation angles are periodic, normalized states lie on spheres and projective spaces, and circuit parameters are coupled through the quantum states they produce. We present a systematic study of how such geometry affects the core operations of DE and SOMA. Keeping the operators and selection rules fixed, we replace only their geometric primitives and separate the effects of difference construction, masking, and selection in a large paired numerical study covering textbook manifolds and variational quantum problems. Geometry-consistent differences make full-crossover (CR = 1) DE significantly better on 16 of 31 non-Euclidean configurations, with no significant deterioration, and the advantage persists when the measured computational cost of each variant is taken into account. The effect is largest where ordinary subtraction misrepresents distances between candidates: success on periodic synchronization rises from 44% to 100%, and on a positive-definite matrix problem from 1% to 99%. On six- qubit variational eigensolvers, shortest-path angular differences reduce the mean final loss by 90% for about 3% extra runtime. The improvements come with two contrasting diversity patterns, more effective population contraction or preserved population diversity, so higher acceptance rates do not necessarily indicate better search. Crossover masks interact with geometry: they can favor cheaper retractions and can increase the distance moved in quantum-state space when circuit parameters are coupled. These results give practical rules for designing population-based optimizers on non-Euclidean and quantum search spaces.
entry.arxiv:comment: Submitted to Swarm and Evolutionary Computation for publication

entry.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence
entry.summary: When LLM agents verify each other's work over a long interaction, they drift into collusion: they come to accept work without the evidence that the verification protocol requires. Collusion is absent at the start and builds up episode by episode, which we trace to accurate feedback accumulating in memory. An agent that follows the rule is told that its verdict was wrong whenever its peer was right, so breaking the rule is the reward-maximizing choice, and agents talk themselves into it in their private reflections. Existing mitigations leave the agents unchanged; we train the behavior out. PROVE (Protocol Reinforcement from Verified Evidence) is a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts by the evidence behind them rather than by their outcome, and credits every call an agent makes, including the calls that solve its own task, with the outcome that call controls. On Qwen3.6-27B, a LoRA adapter trained on six-episode interactions takes the collusion rate on held-out task sequences at the original ten-episode horizon from 65.0% to 1.0%, with no detectable change in task success. Collusion that converged in every interaction now converges in none, and the gain holds four episodes beyond the longest interaction seen in training. The trained 27B model colludes less than every model evaluated in the original study, closed-weight frontier models included. Code is available at https://github.com/Haochen-Luo/PROVE.

entry.title: Compute-Aware Submodular Online Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
entry.summary: This paper studies policy learning for cooperative task allocation in open multi-agent systems, where submodular utilities model diminishing marginal returns due to overlapping agent contributions. While standard methods evaluate every candidate action to update the policy, this may incur an excessive computational cost online. Hence, we impose a budget on these evaluations and analytically study the effect of query budget on online learning. Our algorithm samples a prescribed number of agent-action pairs and applies inverse-probability weighting to their marginal gains, yielding an unbiased gradient estimate of the expected stage utility for a Kullback-Leibler (KL) mirror-ascent update. We derive a $1/2$-approximate regret bound that elegantly splits into a tracking error between optimal and learned policies, quantified by their KL divergence, and a query-dependent feedback term. Experiments on cooperative information coverage show that our approach retains high performance with significantly less computation online.

entry.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding
entry.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate impressive multimodal capabilities, yet suffer from hallucination - generating factually inaccurate content. Contrastive Decoding (CD) mitigates this by contrasting amateur and expert branches at the logit level. However, our investigation reveals that such logit-level interventions fundamentally compromise generation coherence, necessitating restrictive penalty constraints unrelated to hallucination suppression. We introduce Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), a training-free plug-in that complements logit-level CD by relocating part of the contrastive operations to the attention mechanism. Operating at an earlier stage of the forward pass, ACD performs smooth semantic-preserving interventions through an Adaptive Subtraction Strategy (ASS), which attenuates hallucination-associated attention patterns while amplifying critical visual information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that combining ACD with existing CD methods (e.g., VCD+ACD) produces substantially more coherent outputs with further reduced hallucinations, eliminating restrictive penalties while enabling trustworthy multimodal generation.

entry.title: Text-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models for Multimodal Forecasting
entry.summary: Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) provide transferable numerical forecasting priors. However, forecast-relevant information may be conveyed in text without being reflected in the observed series. Many multimodal forecasting methods integrate such context through model inputs or intermediate representations. We investigate a complementary mechanism: text-conditioned parameter adaptation. We propose Context-to-LoRA for Time Series (C2LoRA-TS), which encodes text and generates temporary Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) updates for selected weight matrices of a frozen TSFM. Both the numerical backbone and text encoder remain frozen, and the method exactly recovers the frozen TSFM output when context is absent. Evaluated on Time-MMD across nine domains and three TSFM architectures, C2LoRA-TS achieves lower aggregate forecasting error than the frozen-TSFM and Static LoRA baselines for every architecture and seed. Replacing the instance-specific text with a single globally fixed context degrades performance for every architecture. These results support text-conditioned parameter generation as a viable strategy for multimodal forecasting with frozen TSFMs.
entry.arxiv:comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems: From Forecasting to World Modeling (FMTS 2026)

entry.title: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
entry.summary: Quantum reflection is a counter-intuitive process occurring when an atom is reflected by a rapidly-varying attraction towards a surface, for example the Casimir-Polder force. The reflection probability depends on the attractive potential and on the mass of the atom. For hydrogen isotopes, the potentials are nearly identical whereas significant differences in quantum reflection come from the effect of atomic mass. We calculate the quantum reflection probability for the three isotopes H, D or T falling onto the plane surface of an intrinsic silicon bulk. We show that the results obey scaling laws determined by scattering lengths calculated from theory. Moreover the scattering lengths also obey scaling laws with respect to atomic masses of the isotopes.

entry.title: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
entry.summary: Providers watermark the outputs of large language models, while applications sample many responses per prompt for self-consistency, best-of-n selection, and uncertainty estimation. We show that deployed configurations of distortion-free watermarks, which deduplicate keyed contexts only within a response, couple the responses of a request: answer templates make all responses query the watermark with the same context before the answer, so collisions across responses, usually assumed rare, become the norm. Key pools reduce or avoid the coupling at the cost of multiple testing, and the exact remedy of a context history shared across the request leaves many positions unwatermarked. We propose SOLO, which keeps a request-scoped context history but anchors its keyed contexts on content selected by min-hash, so that siblings rarely compete for a context and random edits stay local. Its responses are jointly distributed as independent unwatermarked responses, each detectable with a single key. On five language models from three families and three benchmarks, SOLO preserves self-consistency and uncertainty estimation and, at a 1% false positive rate, detects more responses than four-token key pools on most tasks, also after randomly editing 10% of the tokens, and more than the context history on most clean tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhongliangGuo/solo-watermark.

entry.title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
entry.summary: Existing defenses against indirect prompt injection in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are inherently reactive: prompt-engineering methods are often overridden by the injected instructions, while supervised detectors must be retrained for each new attack style. We propose a different paradigm: defend by maximizing relevance, not by detecting attacks. Our method, MINE, is training-free and attack-agnostic, and it also serves as a query-conditioned reranker. To evaluate defenses under realistic conditions, we introduce LC-Inj-SQuAD, a long-context benchmark with an average of 4,032 words per context. We evaluate on four datasets spanning short-context QA (Inj-SQuAD, Inj-TriviaQA), long-context QA (LC-Inj-SQuAD), and agent tool-call injection (InjecAgent). Across all four, MINE achieves the best accuracy--security trade-off among training-free defenses. It is also the only defense that stays usable against a fully adaptive attacker, generalizes to agent tool-call injection, and achieves the lowest inference latency on long contexts.
entry.arxiv:comment: To appear in Proceedings of EACL 2027 (Main conference paper)

entry.title: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities
entry.summary: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) in real-world systems must handle unpredictable modality missingness caused by sensor failures, privacy masking, and unstable transmission. Existing methods either learn reliability-aware representations or reconstruct missing inputs, often using a single flattened encoder output. This overlooks deep encoders' semantic hierarchy and intra- and inter-modal interactions, causing semantic averaging and ill-posed mappings. We propose Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL), a framework that exploits semantic hierarchy for robust MSA with missing modalities. Hierarchical Semantic Decoupling exposes low-, mid-, and high-level feature streams from each modality encoder. Cross-Modal Cross-Level Semantic Reconstruction performs ladder-style recovery, using high-level semantics from observed modalities as global anchors to progressively reconstruct mid-level structures and low-level details of missing modalities. To stabilize cross-level reconstruction, Hierarchical Cascade Error Supervisor applies prototypical contrastive regularization to observed and reconstructed features, enforcing level-specific semantic consistency and limiting error propagation. Finally, Hierarchical Interactive Fusion captures dense interactions across modalities and semantic levels to produce robust predictions under diverse missingness patterns. Experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, IEMOCAP, and CH-SIMS show that HSL outperforms baselines in most missing-modality settings.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted for Publication in IEEE Transactions on Multimedia (TMM), 2026

entry.title: Agentic-Level Adversarial Purification: Revisiting Diffusion Purifiers on Native-Resolution Agentic Inputs
entry.summary: Vision-language agents act on native-resolution renders of multi-element pages, where one perturbed photo or a few altered text strokes can redirect the decision. Any content provider can craft such a perturbation on the open model behind the agent, so a plug-in purifier is the natural first line of defense. Yet diffusion purifiers were designed and evaluated at the fixed resolution of the diffusion model on classifier or natural-image benchmarks, and defense evaluations for agents test JPEG, blur and noise but no diffusion purifier. We present the first study of adversarial purification at the agentic level, for an agent built on Qwen3-VL-8B: purifiers run at native resolution on multi-element inputs, face grey-box attackers who know the agent's model but not the defense, and are compared at matched clean cost. We show that treating agentic inputs as classifier inputs misleads both evaluation and design. Resizing the input to the resolution of the diffusion model, as existing purifiers do, raises the TextVQA clean cost of the Divide-and-Conquer purifier (DC) from 4.0 to 35.7 points. On web-shop pages, DC keeps 85.0% grey-box robust accuracy against web-hardened perturbations, where cheap input transformations at matched clean cost keep at most 40.0%, and this robustness comes from the global noise level: input-estimated masks and noise levels add none. These findings hold on a disjoint held-out set and on a second VLM and yield three requirements for defenses, we release the protocol.

entry.title: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model
entry.summary: Within the standard prepare-measure framework, it has been demonstrated that certain compositions of two elementary quantum systems can produce beyond-quantum correlations and can even lead to perfect discrimination of two non-orthogonal quantum states. In this Letter, we introduce the pseudo-quantum model (PQM) for a single system that incorporates the \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} (they satisfy all the properties of quantum states and effects except having negative eigenvalues), and yields valid probability. We consider a prepare-measure communication game known as random access code (RAC) and demonstrate that the success probability achievable within PQM exceeds the corresponding optimal quantum success probability, thereby giving rise to beyond-quantum correlations even for a single system. We then show that such correlations are unphysical as they violate the information causality (IC) principle. Moreover, we demonstrate that two non-orthogonal states can be perfectly distinguishable in PQM for a single system. Therefore, we demonstrate that for a single indivisible system (devoid of any composition), the negativity of \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} can lead to the emergence of beyond-quantum correlations.

entry.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
entry.summary: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. We tested whether resting-state and task-based functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) could identify neurophysiological subgroups alongside clinical assessment.Seventy-nine patients underwent unsupervised clustering using three fNIRS feature views: resting-state activity and connectivity, language-task activation, and rest-to-task connectivity reconfiguration. Similarity network fusion and spectral clustering integrated the views. Clinical and behavioural measures were excluded from clustering.Three clusters (n = 32, 17 and 30) were identified. This solution had the largest eigengap and was the only candidate significant after permutation testing and Holm correction (adjusted P = 0.001). It was stable under subsampling (mean adjusted Rand index, 0.773), but agreement fell to 0.217 when the resting-state view was removed. Clusters differed in most regional intrinsic-activity measures and all resting-state connectivity summaries, with few differences in task activation or connectivity reconfiguration. Their profiles showed higher right anterior prefrontal activity, distributed fronto-sensorimotor and parietal alterations, and reduced interhemispheric connectivity, respectively.Cluster membership was not significantly associated with conventional aphasia subtype (Cramér's V = 0.287), and baseline clinical language scores and task performance did not differ between clusters.These findings identify three neurophysiological subgroups distinguished mainly by intrinsic activity and resting-state functional connectivity, not clearly aligned with conventional aphasia classifications or baseline clinical measures. Multi-view fNIRS analysis may complement clinical characterisation, requiring independent and longitudinal validation.
entry.arxiv:comment: 30 pages, 4 tables, 7 figures

entry.title: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine
entry.summary: Mapping optimization problems to the restricted coefficient range of an 8-bit CIM can distort their encoded energy landscapes. We investigate whether three coefficient-range mitigation techniques previously studied for quantum annealing---interaction extension, bounded-coefficient encoding, and augmented Lagrangian penalties---improve end-to-end optimization outcomes. Experiments on weighted Max-Cut, multidimensional knapsack, and quadratic assignment show that the benefits are selective. At a fixed number of CIM calls, intermediate interaction extension yields higher mean best Max-Cut objectives, whereas aggressive extension degrades performance. Bounded-coefficient encoding improves the mean best feasible profit on one knapsack instance but not the other. Augmented Lagrangian perturbations increase feasibility when unshifted constraint penalties are too weak, but do not outperform the best unshifted penalty setting. Overall, coefficient-range mitigation is most effective when its strength is tuned to the problem and encoding, with aggressive mitigation potentially offsetting its benefits.
entry.arxiv:comment: 42 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables

entry.title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
entry.summary: Single-cell-informed deconvolution provides cell-type-resolved features for clinical bulk RNA cohorts. Most existing methods predict the proportions $π_k$ of the $K$ constituent cell types (CTs). Fewer predict cell-type-specific expression (CTSE) $μ_{kg}$ of gene $g$ in CT $k$, which can capture cell states that proportions miss, but recent benchmarks find it much harder. We explain this gap with closed-form accuracy bounds. For CTSE, we derive an $R^2$ ceiling for per-gene linear estimators. For proportions, the best linear estimator, which pools evidence across genes, has a closed-form $R^2$, and a computable lower bound on it predicts which CTs are learnable. We study targeted deconvolution of 106 biologically curated (CT, gene) pairs, found post hoc to have higher learnability scores. On overall survival in non-small cell lung cancer, estimation difficulty does not predict prognostic value across these targets. Yet a sparse survival model on deconvolved features, mostly CTSE, predicts survival as well as a sparse model on the bulk genes themselves, while attributing its signal to specific cell types. Some deconvolved CTSE features reveal prognostic signal not seen in the corresponding bulk gene.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD). 5 pages main text, 28 pages total

entry.title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
entry.summary: Task allocation in contested-objective team games requires coordinated decisions under uncertainty, spatial constraints, and changing tactical conditions. In such settings, multiple agents must anticipate both teammate behavior and opponent actions. We study a hybrid predict-then-optimize approach for assigning controllable agents to objectives in real time. A masked multi-head model predicts tactical signals for each agent, including survival chance, local superiority, combat interaction, travel time, and objective contribution. These signals are combined with rule-based terms in a score matrix, and a minimum-cost flow solver computes coordinated global assignments constrained by capacity, occupancy, stability, and defensive strategies. Learning is limited to tactical scoring, while explicit rules and solver structure preserve controllability and interpretability. We evaluate the system using predictive metrics, offline assignment diagnostics, online A/B evaluation, and latency measurements. The system is an R\&D research prototype built on a commercial game and is not deployed in the shipped game. The results indicate that learned tactical estimates can support stable, feasible, and inspectable objective allocation under strict real-time constraints.

entry.title: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents
entry.summary: Amine-impregnated sorbents with the highest nominal CO2 capacity are frequently the least deployable, as amine beyond the pore-volume limit blocks active sites. Yet multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) for direct air capture (DAC) treats formulation search as unconstrained. We encode the pore-filling boundary as an explicit outcome constraint, c(x) = tanh(1 - phi_hat) - tau, and use it as a diagnostic instrument on a hand-curated, DOI-traceable benchmark of 618 solid-amine formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained MOBO attains higher nominal capacity (3.639 +/- 0.815 vs. 2.964 +/- 0.728 mmol/g, p = 1.0e-11), but across 100 seeds 63.2% of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary versus 39.3% under the constraint: it is rewarded for proposing candidates outside the pore-confined design regime. The constraint steers the front to lower loadings (55.8 vs. 65.2 wt%) and larger pores. The boundary is corroborated once apparatus effects are harmonized hierarchically: 77.8% of kinetic variance is between-laboratory, and pore filling carries a significant kinetic penalty (p = 0.002). Standard hypervolume over-credits feasibility-agnostic methods by 13.9-16.1% (vs. 11.1% constrained), and three surrogate-based analyses---the constrained front, a regeneration-energy third objective, and harmonized kinetics---consistently point to a conservative deployable window at pore filling phi_hat ~ 0.4-0.5 (45-55 wt% loading). The benchmark and associated analysis outputs accompany this submission.
